title: Project Discovery & Planning
outcome: Define the project problem, identify users/tasks, and structure the site architecture.
before: A website idea only; no project evidence or code structure exists.
after: A documented project plan and repository scaffold ready for semantic HTML.
core: Plan the problem, the users and the content before choosing colours or writing HTML.
concepts: Guide feature decisions before code is written.
Represent realistic users, needs and tasks.
Plan page structure and layout before implementation.
tasks: Write five user stories with acceptance checks
Draw the sitemap and homepage wireframe
tests: Check user stories include user, goal and reason
Confirm the sitemap matches the planned pages

title: HTML Foundation & Semantic Structure
outcome: Create meaningful page regions and build web pages using appropriate structural elements.
before: Week 01 produced the sitemap, wireframe and repository scaffold.
after: A semantic HTML skeleton using header, nav, main, section, footer and a clear document outline.
core: HTML should describe the meaning and structure of the content before CSS changes the appearance.
concepts: Provides the page with a valid HTML base.
Name page regions by purpose rather than appearance.
Creates a logical document outline for users and assistive technology.
tasks: Translate wireframe regions into semantic elements
Add placeholder content for hero, cards and footer
tests: Check navigation links point to planned pages

title: Forms & Visual Design Basics
outcome: Implement user data collection and apply visual design principles to control user attention.
before: Week 02 created a semantic homepage and page regions.
after: The site collects trip-planning information and has a clear visual hierarchy.
core: Forms are conversations with users; visual design should make that conversation easy to follow.
concepts: Connect visible meaning to each input.
Improve mobile keyboards, validation and user experience.
Typography, colour and spacing guide attention.
tasks: Create the Plan a Trip form
Use labels and suitable input types
Add required fields and helpful placeholder text
tests: Check every input has a visible label
codeA:
<label for="visitorName">Your name</label>
<input id="visitorName" name="visitorName" type="text" required>
next: Week 04 uses Flexbox and Grid to organise navigation, forms and card galleries.
milestone: Trip form plus typography, colour and spacing system
commit: Complete Week 03 forms and visual design

title: Layout Systems (Flexbox & Grid)
outcome: Manage one-dimensional and two-dimensional layouts for complex page sections.
before: Week 03 produced forms and a basic visual design system.
after: The website uses intentional layout systems for navigation, forms, cards and page sections.
core: Use Flexbox for one-dimensional alignment and Grid for two-dimensional page and card structures.
concepts: Aligns items along one main axis.
Adds maintainable spacing without margin hacks.
tasks: Convert navigation into a Flexbox row
Align form controls with consistent gap
Create a card gallery with CSS Grid
Use container width to improve readability
tests: Confirm form labels align with controls
next: Week 05 adapts these layouts for mobile, tablet and desktop using responsive design.
milestone: Flexbox navigation, aligned forms and Grid destination cards
commit: Complete Week 04 Flexbox and Grid layouts

title: Responsive Design
outcome: Adapt the website interface to function across various device screen sizes.
before: Week 04 created structured layouts using Flexbox and Grid.
after: The interface adapts cleanly across mobile, tablet and desktop widths.
core: Start with flexible layouts and add breakpoints when the layout needs help, not because of a device name.
concepts: Starts with the simplest layout and progressively enhances it.
Apply layout changes at meaningful widths.
Prevents images and grids from forcing horizontal scroll.
tasks: Stack navigation and cards on small screens
Test the main user journey at several widths
tests: Check tap targets and line length
next: Week 06 adds JavaScript and DOM interaction to the responsive interface.

title: JavaScript & DOM Interaction
outcome: Add behaviour to a page by connecting programming logic to user actions via the DOM.
before: Week 05 produced a responsive interface ready for interaction.
after: Navigation and interface components respond to user actions through JavaScript.
core: Use JavaScript to listen for events, update state and change the interface deliberately.
concepts: The browser's object model of the page.
Keeps behaviour in JavaScript and styling in CSS.
tasks: Add DOM hooks to the navigation
Write an event listener for the mobile menu
Toggle a state class instead of inline styles
Add a simple theme or FAQ interaction
Test interaction with click and keyboard focus
tests: Verify the site still works if JavaScript fails gracefully
next: Week 07 strengthens forms with validation and stores lightweight choices in the browser.
milestone: Interactive mobile navigation and state-based UI behaviour

title: Advanced Forms & Storage
outcome: Implement client-side validation and persist lightweight user choices between browser sessions.
before: Week 06 added DOM interaction and state changes.
after: Forms provide clear validation feedback and lightweight preferences can persist across visits.
core: Validate close to the user and store only lightweight, non-sensitive values in browser storage.
concepts: Improves feedback but does not replace server-side validation.
Stores string values across browser sessions.
Avoids private, secret or sensitive information in the browser.
tasks: Prevent submission when required logic fails
Save theme choice or favourite destination IDs
Recover saved values on page load
tests: Refresh the browser and check saved preferences
Clear storage and retest default state
Check storage does not contain private data
next: Week 08 loads destination and event content from JSON using the Fetch API.
milestone: Validation feedback plus persisted lightweight preferences

title: Dynamic Data & Fetch API
outcome: Decouple content from structure by loading and rendering dynamic external data.
before: Week 07 added validation and saved lightweight user choices.
after: Destination and event content is loaded from JSON and rendered dynamically.
core: Store repeatable content as data, fetch it, then render the interface from that data.
concepts: Represents structured content independently from HTML.
Transforms data before rendering it into the interface.
tasks: Fetch the JSON file from JavaScript
tests: Run through a local web server
Break the JSON path and observe the error state
Check rendered cards preserve accessibility labels
next: Week 09 checks usability, accessibility and the quality of the interactive site.
milestone: JSON-backed destination cards, filters, loading and error states
commit: Complete Week 08 dynamic data and Fetch API

title: UX, Accessibility & Testing
outcome: Ensure the site is usable for people with different abilities and optimized for interface quality.
before: Week 08 created dynamic data rendering and filtering.
after: The site has clearer labels, keyboard focus, accessible interactive states and documented quality checks.
core: Accessibility is not an optional add-on; it is part of professional interface quality.
concepts: Provides built-in accessibility when used correctly.
Shows keyboard users where interaction currently is.
Checks errors and edge cases, not only successful use.
tasks: Add or confirm labels and alt text
Test the journey using keyboard only
tests: Use Lighthouse or a manual checklist
Confirm errors are visible and understandable
next: Week 10 returns to Web Storage in more depth and refines saved preferences.
milestone: Keyboard support, accessible labels/focus and quality evidence
commit: Complete Week 09 accessibility and UX testing

title: Web Storage
outcome: Persist lightweight user preferences between browser sessions.
before: Week 09 identified usability and accessibility issues in the interactive site.
after: Favourites and preferences persist safely and recover from missing or corrupted values.
core: Browser storage is useful for convenience, but it must be small, safe and recoverable.
concepts: Lasts only for the current browser session.
Converts stored strings back into arrays or objects safely.
tasks: Restore saved theme on page load
Handle missing or corrupted storage safely
tests: Verify sensitive data is not stored
next: Week 11 strengthens data rendering and filters using the stored IDs and JSON content.
milestone: Persistent favourites/theme with safe recovery and reset

title: Data Rendering
outcome: Load and render dynamic content from external data sources.
before: Week 10 persisted favourites and preferences using Web Storage.
after: Dynamic content is filtered, rendered consistently, and explains empty/error states.
core: Data rendering is a pipeline: fetch, validate, transform, render and handle failure.
concepts: Selects only data matching the current query or category.
Create consistent repeated HTML from data.
Explain what happened when no result or load failure occurs.
tasks: Add filter controls and empty states
tests: Disable or rename the JSON file
Confirm the UI explains loading and errors
next: Week 12 performs structured UX and testing checks before release.
milestone: Reusable rendering function, filtering and robust interface states

title: UX & Testing
outcome: Ensure the site is accessible, validated and optimized for performance.
before: Week 11 completed dynamic data rendering and filter behaviour.
after: The project has structured test evidence, validation results and documented fixes.
core: Professional release requires evidence: tests, screenshots, validation reports and fixes.
concepts: Checks what users actually do across the interface.
Finds code errors browsers may otherwise tolerate.
Treat accessibility and performance as release criteria.
tasks: Record fixes in a test report
tests: Run Lighthouse or manual accessibility checks

after: The project is uploaded, documented, deployed and ready for final demonstration/code defence.

concepts: Documents purpose, structure and running instructions.
Reveals path, asset and integration issues that local testing can miss.

tests: Trace final features back to Week 01 user stories
